finding: The selected governing reference specs/request-consistency.md#requirements (subject Spec Requirement, line 21) has no matching Input snapshot in the request. The acceptance criterion that requires promotion request binding to be checked (subject line 25), and the promotion runtime requirement that Readiness confirms artifact.requestId equals immutable request.requestId and that inputPath equals the request-bound artifact path (promotion-runtime line 11), both depend on request-binding text that is absent from the supplied inputs. The request binding contract, including the caller-visible outcome when the binding does not hold, cannot be established from the request.

The selected reference specs/image-cache.md#preview-cleanup is not part of this delivery. The What to build section lists only the Validation Report, Result Summary, invalid-input diagnostic wording, indexed cache lookup, single-scan parser strategy, protected access review, promotion, recovery, runtime migration and Reader Index Update behaviors, and states that only those listed behaviors are delivered. The cited requirement, a 24-hour cleanup of image previews that does not change the reader index, does not define an input for any listed behavior. Appearing in Spec Requirement does not make it a delivery input, so this selection is unrelated and cannot expand or authorize scope.

The caller-visible successful result of promote(inputPath) is defined in two incompatible ways across selected requirements. specs/runtime-migration.md states that the successful result is exactly {status: 'succeeded', artifactId, trackedStateId}, while specs/result-summary.md requires the same successful result to include a string summary whose value is '${artifactId} promoted to ${trackedStateId}'. Both are selected for this issue, so the delivered public success shape is not determined.

The caller-visible expected filesystem failure is defined with incompatible field sets. specs/runtime-migration.md states that it is exactly {recovered: false, failureCode, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus} and defers only the failure value semantics to Promotion Runtime, while specs/promotion-runtime.md defines the same expected filesystem failure as {recovered: false, failureCode, operation, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}, where operation identifies the failed read, precondition or baseline-write step. The public failure shape delivered by promote(inputPath) is therefore not determined.

Whether the selected conditional requirement specs/export-retention.md#conditional-export-retention is delivery content cannot be determined from the request. Reader Index Update points the reader link to docs/reference/validation-report.md. The export-retention requirement applies only if that target is a generated artifact; then the exposure is an artifact export that must follow ADR 0005 with a 30-day duration. If the target is a manually maintained document, the section does not apply. The supplied architecture excerpt says only that this stable replacement target already exists, and no supplied input states whether it is generated or manually maintained. ADR 0005 also scopes its authority to 'promotion artifact retention', so the request does not establish that ADR 0005 is the applicable authority for an export of this target. Whether the export obligation applies therefore depends on an unknown fact.

The selected 30-day retention requirement has no executable owner and no defined observable behavior. specs/promotion-runtime.md says a successful tracked artifact is kept for 30 days from the successful tracked commit, that removal after expiry is not part of this operation, and that downstream persistence only consumes the applied selection. The persistence interface receives retentionDays and says persistence consumes it, but no supplied text defines what persistence does with the value, and no selected requirement assigns expiry removal to any Module. The duration obligation from ADR 0005 therefore cannot be implemented or verified as retention behavior; the acceptance criterion reduces it to a source-review check of the value passed.

The selected authorization requirement does not bind the resource that is read. specs/access-review.md states that the policy is {policyId, allowedOperations} and that the decision is made only by operation, while the facts include resourceId. Its Module Design text makes request.resourceId the source passed to the existing readArtifact(source) after an allowed decision. As written, any verified principal whose request names an allowed operation can cause any resourceId that the Reader accepts to be read, because no selected requirement restricts which resources an authorized operation may name. The authorization outcome for protected reads is therefore not determined by the selected requirement.
